text: Which number, written out in English as a word, is the only one whose letters run in alphabetical order?
why: F, O, R, T, Y: each letter comes later in the alphabet than the one before, and no other number word does that.

text: In a family, each girl has as many brothers as sisters, but each boy has twice as many sisters as brothers. How many children are in the family?
why: Four girls and three boys: a girl has 3 sisters and 3 brothers; a boy has 2 brothers and 4 sisters.

text: Counting squares of every size, how many squares are there on a chessboard?
why: 64 one-by-one, 49 two-by-two, 36, 25, 16, 9, 4 and 1 eight-by-eight: 204 in all.

text: Which letter of the alphabet does not appear in the name of any of the 50 US states?
why: Every other letter turns up somewhere, even J (New Jersey), X (Texas) and Z (Arizona), but no state has a Q.
They are the square numbers written backwards: 16 becomes 61, 25 becomes 52, and 64 becomes 46.

text: Which two-digit number is exactly twice the product of its two digits?
why: 3 × 6 = 18, and 18 × 2 = 36. No other two-digit number works.

text: Find a four-digit number whose first digit is how many 0s it contains, its second digit how many 1s, its third how many 2s and its fourth how many 3s.
why: 1210 has one 0, two 1s, one 2 and no 3s. (2020 works too: two 0s, no 1s, two 2s, no 3s.)

text: The letters of ELEVEN PLUS TWO can be rearranged into another sum with the same answer. What is it?
why: TWELVE PLUS ONE uses exactly the same thirteen letters, and both sums make 13.

text: The day before yesterday I was 25. Next year I will be 28. What is today's date?
why: My birthday is 31 December. On 30 December I was 25, I turned 26 yesterday, I turn 27 at the end of this year and 28 next year.

text: Which English word is still pronounced exactly the same after you take away its last four letters?
why: QUEUE without U-E-U-E leaves Q, which sounds just the same.

text: A clock shows exactly 3:15. What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand, in degrees?
why: The minute hand points at the 3, but by quarter past the hour hand has moved a quarter of the way to the 4: a quarter of 30° is 7.5°.

text: A clock takes 5 seconds to strike six o'clock. How many seconds does it take to strike twelve?
why: Six strikes have five gaps, one second each. Twelve strikes have eleven gaps: 11 seconds.

text: Which whole number from one to ten, spelled out, has its letters in reverse alphabetical order?
why: O, N, E: each letter comes earlier in the alphabet than the one before. None of the others manages it.

text: On an old calculator, which number do you type so that the display turned upside down reads 'hELLO'?
why: 0.7734 upside down: 4 looks like h, 3 like E, the 7s like Ls and 0 like O.

text: Which is the only common English word that ends in the letters 'mt'?
why: Dreamt (and undreamt, which is the same word with a prefix).

text: If you write out every whole number from 1 to 100, how many times do you write the digit 7?
why: Ten times as a last digit (7, 17 … 97) and ten times as a first digit (70 to 79). 77 has two of them, so that's 20.

text: Which planet in our Solar System is the only one not named after a god from Greek or Roman mythology?
why: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune are all gods. Earth comes from an Old English word for the ground.

text: Between midday and midnight, how many times do the hour and minute hands of a clock point in exactly the same direction? (Count midday but not midnight.)
why: The minute hand laps the hour hand every 12/11 of an hour, so it catches it 11 times in 12 hours, not 12.

text: Which is the only number that has as many letters as its value when written in English?
why: F-O-U-R has four letters. No other number word matches its own value.

text: Write the numbers one to twenty as words and sort them into alphabetical order. Which comes first?
why: Eight comes before eighteen, eleven, fifteen, five and the rest.

text: How many times can you subtract 10 from 100?
why: Only once: after that you are subtracting from 90, not 100.

text: Which two-digit number has digits that add up to 11, and gets 9 bigger when you swap its digits round?
A nurse gives you three pills and tells you to take one every half an hour. How many minutes will the pills last?
why: The first goes now, the second after 30 minutes and the third after 60.

text: Writing numbers out in British English, what is the smallest whole number whose name contains the letter A?
why: Nothing from one to ninety-nine has an A, and neither does 'one hundred'. The first A is the 'and' in 'one hundred AND one'.

text: What do you get if you add up every number on a roulette wheel, from 0 to 36?
why: Pair them up: 1 + 36, 2 + 35 and so on make 18 pairs of 37, which is 666 (the 0 adds nothing).

text: A man pushes his car up to a hotel and tells the owner he is bankrupt. What is he doing?
why: He's playing Monopoly: his token is the car, and he has landed on a hotel he can't afford.
